accepted.s: What was the status of the Election Commission of India during January 1990?
o: It was replaced by the State Election Commissions
The posts of Election Commissioners were abolished and it became a single-member body again
Its functions were transferred to the Law Commission
It functioned with the CEC and two Election Commissioners
accepted.x: In January 1990, the posts of the additional Election Commissioners were abolished and the Election Commission again became a single-member body.
accepted.tq: Test the short-lived institutional reversal between the 1989 expansion and the later multi-member arrangement.
accepted.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India:
1. Since October 1993, it has functioned as a multi-member body consisting of the CEC and two Election Commissioners.
2. Decisions in the multi-member Commission are taken by majority.
3. The Chief Election Commissioner has an absolute veto over every decision of the Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because decisions are governed by the majority rule and the CEC does not possess an absolute veto over every decision.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute-power statement and identify the majority-rule principle.
accepted.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

accepted.s: The constitutional validity of the multi-member Election Commission and the majority rule was upheld in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
ADR v. Election Commission of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
accepted.x: The Supreme Court upheld the multi-member structure and majority rule in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995).
accepted.tq: Use the case-name association to distinguish institutional-structure litigation from election-process cases.
accepted.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the election reforms of the T.N. Seshan era?
o: Transfer of election petitions from High Courts to the Election Commission
Strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct in 1991
Introduction of Electors Photo Identity Cards
accepted.x: Election petitions were not transferred to the Election Commission; they are tried by the High Courts in the case of Parliamentary and State Legislature elections. The other three measures were associated with the Seshan era.
accepted.tq: Find the institutional power wrongly transferred to the Election Commission.
accepted.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

accepted.s: During the enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct in 1991, which action was associated with the T.N. Seshan era?
o: All political parties were dissolved by the President
Voting was restricted to holders of Electors Photo Identity Cards
Politicians violating the Code were arrested and partisan police officers were removed
Election petitions were decided by the Election Commission
accepted.x: The Seshan-era enforcement included arresting politicians who violated the Model Code of Conduct and removing partisan police officers.
accepted.tq: Match the reformer with the specific enforcement actions rather than with unrelated constitutional powers.
accepted.sec: Multi-member commission history - T.N. Seshan era reforms

accepted.s:
With reference to Article 329 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. Laws relating to delimitation of constituencies cannot be questioned in any court.
2. The allotment of seats to constituencies cannot be questioned in any court.
3. An election to Parliament or a State Legislature can be questioned only through an election petition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 329(a) bars judicial challenge to laws relating to delimitation and allotment of seats, while Article 329(b) requires an election to be challenged only through an election petition.
accepted.tq: Split Article 329 into its two clauses and test both the delimitation bar and the election-petition rule.
accepted.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

accepted.s: An election to Parliament or a State Legislature may be challenged under Article 329(b) through an election petition under which law?
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Representation of the People Act, 1950
accepted.x: Article 329(b) operates with the election-petition mechanism provided under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two Representation of the People Acts by linking election petitions with the 1951 Act.
accepted.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the judicial forum and appellate route for an election petition concerning a Parliamentary or State Legislative election?
o: It is tried by the Election Commission, with appeal to the High Court
It is tried by the Governor, with appeal to the Election Commission
It is tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court
It is tried directly by the Supreme Court, with appeal to the President
accepted.x: Election petitions concerning Parliament or State Legislatures are tried by the High Court, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to separate the Election Commission from the judicial forum.
accepted.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

accepted.s: Which one of the following functions is performed by the Election Commission of India rather than by a court hearing an election petition?
o: Adjudicating disputes concerning the election of the President under Article 71
Hearing an appeal from a High Court judgment in an election petition
Deciding disputes relating to political parties and election symbols
accepted.x: The Election Commission decides disputes concerning political parties and election symbols and advises on disqualification. It does not try election petitions or decide presidential election disputes.
accepted.tq: Separate the Commission's administrative and quasi-judicial functions from the courts' election-petition jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. By convention, courts generally do not interfere once the election process has begun.
2. The Election Commission can review the result of an election after it has been declared.
3. The Election Commission does not try election petitions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the Election Commission cannot review an election result; challenges must follow the election-petition route.
accepted.tq: Use the negative institutional-power trap: the Commission conducts elections but does not review declared results or try petitions.
accepted.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Provision)
A. Article 329(a)
B. Article 329(b)
C. Article 71

List-II (Subject)
1. Election disputes concerning President and Vice-President
2. Bar on questioning delimitation and allotment of seats in court
3. Challenge to an election only by an election petition

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Article 329(a) concerns the bar on challenges to delimitation and seat allotment, Article 329(b) requires an election petition, and Article 71 covers disputes regarding Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Article 71 pair and then distinguish the two clauses of Article 329.
accepted.sec: Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Institution or authority)
A. Chief Electoral Officer
B. State Election Commission
C. District Collector
D. Election Commission of India

List-II (Function or position)
1. District Election Officer/District Returning Officer
2. Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
3. Conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
4. State-level officer for elections under the control of the Election Commission of India

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is the state-level officer under the ECI; the SEC conducts local-body elections; the Collector serves as District Election Officer/District Returning Officer; and the ECI conducts Parliamentary and State Legislative elections.
accepted.tq: Build the answer from the sure district-level pair and then separate ECI elections from SEC elections.
accepted.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

accepted.s: The Chief Electoral Officer of a State is appointed by the Election Commission of India from among which category?
o: Senior civil servants of the State
Judges of the concerned High Court
Members of the State Legislative Assembly
accepted.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is appointed by the Election Commission of India from among senior civil servants of the State.
accepted.tq: Test the appointing authority and source cadre together, avoiding confusion with the Governor's appointment of the State Election Commissioner.
accepted.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chief Electoral Officer and the State Election Commission:
1. The Chief Electoral Officer functions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
2. The State Election Commission functions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
3. The Chief Electoral Officer is removed like a High Court judge.
4. The State Election Commissioner is removable only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Chief Electoral Officer is removed by the Election Commission, whereas the State Election Commissioner enjoys protection comparable to that of a High Court judge.
accepted.tq: Compare the two offices line by line, especially the easily swapped removal provisions.
accepted.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

accepted.s: Which of the following elections is conducted by the State Election Commission rather than by the Election Commission of India?
o: Election to a State Legislative Council
accepted.x: Municipal elections, along with Panchayat elections, are conducted by the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
accepted.tq: Use the body-versus-election distinction to identify the local-government election.
accepted.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Election Commission of India — President and Vice-President elections
Election Commission of India — Election of Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly
accepted.x: The Speaker is elected by the House itself, not by the Election Commission of India. The ECI conducts elections to the offices of President and Vice-President, while State Election Commissions conduct Panchayat and municipal elections.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong authority by asking who elects an office from within the House itself.
accepted.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

accepted.s: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner, and what protection governs removal from office?
o: The Election Commission of India; removal at the pleasure of the President
The Governor; removal only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge
The Chief Minister; removal by the State Legislative Assembly
The President; removal by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and can be removed only in the manner applicable to a High Court judge under Article 243K(2).
accepted.tq: Pair the appointing authority with the constitutional removal safeguard instead of confusing it with the CEO's position.
accepted.sec: Chief Electoral Officer of the state and AP State Election Commission - distinction

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Initiative)
A. SVEEP
B. cVIGIL
C. Saksham
D. Voter Helpline

List-II (Purpose)
1. Registration, corrections, roll search and complaints
2. Reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos
3. Voter education and electoral participation
4. Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: SVEEP promotes voter education and turnout; cVIGIL reports Model Code violations; Saksham assists voters with disabilities; and Voter Helpline provides registration, correction, search and complaint services.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive cVIGIL geo-tagging function and eliminate codes that misplace the remaining apps.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

accepted.s: SVEEP, launched in 2009, is primarily associated with which objective?
accepted.x: SVEEP stands for Systematic Voters' Education and Electoral Participation and is a voter education and turnout programme launched in 2009.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with the programme's stated objective and launch year.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

accepted.s: A citizen wants to report a suspected violation of the Model Code of Conduct by uploading a geo-tagged video. Which platform is most appropriate?
accepted.x: cVIGIL enables citizens to report Model Code of Conduct violations using geo-tagged photographs or videos.
accepted.tq: Map the practical scenario to the app whose defining feature is geo-tagged complaint reporting.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Special Intensive Revision is correct?
o: The Bihar SIR removed about 70 lakh names and the subsequent turnout was the highest since Independence.
The Bihar SIR concerned only municipal elections.
The Bihar SIR removed about 7 lakh names and produced the lowest turnout since Independence.
The Bihar SIR was conducted exclusively through the Saksham application.
accepted.x: The Bihar Special Intensive Revision removed about 70 lakh names, and the turnout that followed was reported as the highest since Independence.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the similar figures 7 lakh and 70 lakh and retain the correct turnout comparison.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

accepted.s: Which district in Andhra Pradesh achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of Special Intensive Revision enumeration forms?
accepted.x: ASR district in Andhra Pradesh achieved 100 per cent digitalisation of SIR enumeration forms.
accepted.tq: Test the exact district associated with the complete digitalisation milestone.
accepted.sec: Voter facilitation apps and campaigns

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding VVPAT:
1. It is attached to the Electronic Voting Machine.
2. It prints a slip containing the serial number, name and symbol of the selected candidate.
3. The voter can see the printed slip for seven seconds.
4. The slip is handed over to the voter for personal custody.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the voter views the slip through the VVPAT window; it is not handed over to the voter.
accepted.tq: Use the operational sequence and reject the plausible but incorrect claim that the voter receives the paper slip.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: The use of VVPAT was permitted through an amendment to which rules?
o: The Representation of the People Rules, 1950
accepted.x: VVPAT use was permitted through an amendment to the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact subordinate-rules framework instead of confusing it with the Representation of the People Acts.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: VVPAT was first used in an election at which location in 2013?
accepted.x: VVPAT was first used in 2013 at 51-Noksen in Nagaland. The 70-Parur reference relates to the first EVM pilot in 1982.
accepted.tq: Separate the two easily confused first-use locations: VVPAT at 51-Noksen and EVM pilot at 70-Parur.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: EVMs and VVPATs used by the Election Commission of India are manufactured by which organisations?
accepted.x: Electronic Voting Machines and VVPATs are manufactured by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) and Electronics Corporation of India Limited (ECIL).
accepted.tq: Recall the paired public-sector manufacturers without substituting other electronics or defence organisations.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the early use of Electronic Voting Machines?
o: They were first piloted at 70-Parur, Kerala, in 1982 and used universally in the 2004 Lok Sabha election.
They were first piloted at 51-Noksen, Nagaland, in 2013 and used universally in 2009.
They were first piloted in Delhi in 1991 and used universally in 1996.
They were first piloted in Andhra Pradesh in 1989 and used universally in 1999.
accepted.x: EVMs were first piloted at 70-Parur in Kerala in 1982 and were used universally in the 2004 Lok Sabha election.
accepted.tq: Keep the EVM timeline distinct from the later VVPAT timeline by checking both the location and year.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: Under the Supreme Court's 2019 verification arrangement, how many randomly chosen VVPATs are counted per Assembly segment?
accepted.x: The slips of five randomly chosen VVPATs are counted in each Assembly segment under the Supreme Court's 2019 arrangement.
accepted.tq: Test the prescribed numerical standard directly and distinguish it from the later 100 per cent counting demand.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: Which of the following was the decision of the Supreme Court in ADR v. Election Commission of India in April 2024?
o: It abolished the use of VVPAT machines.
It ordered compulsory counting of 100 per cent of VVPAT slips in every election.
It rejected the demand for 100 per cent VVPAT counting.
It transferred VVPAT verification entirely to State Election Commissions.
accepted.x: In ADR v. ECI (April 2024), the Supreme Court rejected the demand for counting 100 per cent of VVPAT slips.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversal trap involving a demand for total counting and the Court's actual decision.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules

accepted.s: Candidates placed second and third in an election may seek verification of what proportion of EVMs' burnt memory per Assembly segment, and within what period after the result?
accepted.x: Candidates placed second and third may seek verification of 5 per cent of EVMs' burnt memory per Assembly segment within seven days of the result.
accepted.tq: Pair both numerical conditions—percentage and time limit—to avoid selecting an option with only one correct figure.
accepted.sec: VVPAT - working, verification rules
